source_text.body:
Build custom store tools instead of paying for subscriptions
The poster uses Claude Code to build ecommerce tools including support inbox consolidation, a profit dashboard, auto-replies for order-status and returns emails, and abandoned-cart follow-up.
·
May 12, 2026
Done with
CC
Claude Code
What they did
The poster spent the past month using Claude Code to make custom ecommerce tools they would otherwise subscribe to, especially around support, profit tracking, automated order-status and returns replies, and abandoned-cart follow-up. In comments, they explain the setup concretely for Shopify: create a custom app, enable Admin API access, grant scopes like read_orders and read_products, copy the Admin API token, and give that token to Claude Code; another commenter warns to hide the token behind a local script.
How it went
The source gives no hard performance numbers or finished case study results. The main outcome stated is replacing paid app subscriptions with self-built tools, but the thread stays at the idea-and-setup level rather than showing deployed results.
Worth knowing
The clearest catch is access: for Shopify, the key step is creating a custom app and generating an Admin API token; the thread gives no cost breakdown beyond avoiding monthly subscriptions.
Try it yourself
with
Claude Code
Copy prompt
I run an online store on [Shopify/WooCommerce/other]. Build me a simple internal tool that [pick one: merges support emails from [inboxes] into one view / shows daily profit using [data sources] and ad spend / drafts replies to order-status and return emails / follows up on abandoned carts]. Use [language/stack], read data from [API or export], and keep API keys in a config file. The tool is done when it runs locally on my real data and I can see the output. Never send an email or change store data without showing me the draft first.
Original source: https://www.reddit.com/r/ecommerce/comments/1taro12/ive_been_using_claude_code_for_the_past_month_to
